newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate swims higher after low close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate swims higher after low close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 70 basis points at 19.20 percent in early trade on Thursday.
Dealers and analysts said the move owed more to a return to average trading levels, from a late dip on Wednesday, than to higher yields on the U.S. long bond.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile off 4/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper had increased 40 basis points to 19.60 percent.
Liquidity of 1.655 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.

However, an outflow of around 800 million pesos was expected due to general demand for cash. Another 290 million pesos was expected to leave the system after the central bank placed more debt at this week's regular Cetes auction than the amount rolling off.
